title: FI - Domain
topic: Domain knowledge for building a fixed-income fork-based risk engine: curves, risk measures, Treasuries/futures/SOFR swaps, carry and roll, liquidity, scenarios, hedging and optimization, data operations, and model-risk governance

concepts.title: Curves and conventions
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover: day count conventions — ACT/ACT (ICMA) for Treasuries, ACT/360 for SOFR legs, 30/360 for fixed swap legs. Business-day calendars and roll rules: US Government Securities calendar, SIFMA early closes, modified following. Accrued interest, clean vs dirty price, settlement (T+1 for Treasuries). Par, zero, and forward curves, and converting between them. Curve bootstrapping: instrument selection, interpolation choices (log-linear discount, monotone convex) and their effect on forwards. SOFR OIS curve as the discounting curve; Treasury curve construction from on-the-runs vs a fitted spline. QuantLib building blocks: YieldTermStructure, RelinkableHandle, SimpleQuote, observers and lazy recalculation.

concepts.title: Risk measures
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover: DV01 / PV01 — definition, sign conventions, per-position vs portfolio aggregation. Key-rate DV01: choosing buckets, bumping par vs zero rates, triangular vs bucket shifts. Bump-and-reprice vs analytic sensitivities; bump size and central differences. Convexity and why DV01 alone mis-states large shocks. Scenario P&L: full revaluation vs a sensitivity (Taylor) approximation, and when each is acceptable. Curve-shape shocks: parallel, steepener, flattener, butterfly; bull vs bear moves. P&L attribution basics: carry, roll-down, curve move, spread, residual.

concepts.title: Instruments: Treasuries, futures, SOFR swaps
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover — Treasuries: on-the-run vs off-the-run and the liquidity premium between them; bills, notes, bonds, STRIPS; auction cycle and when-issued trading. Treasury futures (TU, FV, TY, US, UB, WN): deliverable basket, conversion factors, cheapest-to-deliver (CTD); futures DV01 = CTD DV01 / conversion factor; CTD switch risk; gross and net basis, implied repo, delivery options; contract specs, quarterly rolls, roll timing. SOFR swaps: fixed vs compounded SOFR legs; payment lag, conventions; cleared (CME/LCH) vs bilateral; initial margin basics; swap spreads vs Treasuries and why they move.

concepts.title: Carry, roll and funding
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover: carry — coupon accrual minus financing cost over a horizon. Roll-down: price change from aging along an unchanged curve. Repo financing: GC vs specials, term repo, how specialness affects carry. Carry of futures (implied repo) and swaps (fixed vs expected floating). 'Carry drag' of a hedge: what it means to a trader and how to express it per month. Forward-starting analysis: rolling a fork forward in time (the engine's time-roll shock).

concepts.title: Liquidity and transaction costs
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover: bid-ask spreads by instrument — on-the-runs vs off-the-runs, futures, swaps. Market depth, average daily volume (ADV), and market impact for size. Building a liquidity score: which inputs, how to normalize, how to keep it explainable. Transaction cost analysis (TCA) and where desks get the data (dealer runs, TRACE for Treasuries, internal fills). Execution venues: dealer-to-client (Tradeweb, Bloomberg) vs interdealer (BrokerTec), CME for futures. Futures contract rounding and minimum sizes.

concepts.title: Scenarios and the macro context
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover: FOMC mechanics — meeting calendar, statement, dot plot, press conference; how the front end vs long end react. 'Hawkish' and 'dovish' translated into curve moves (bear flattener, bull steepener). Other event drivers: CPI, payrolls, Treasury refunding announcements, auctions. Historical scenarios: replaying past moves (e.g. 2013 taper tantrum, 2022 hiking cycle). Hypothetical scenario design: plausibility, consistency across tenors, using PCA (level, slope, curvature). Regulatory stress concepts (CCAR / DFAST rate scenarios) as a vocabulary for bank buyers.

concepts.title: Hedging and optimization
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover: DV01-neutral vs key-rate-matched hedges; hedge ratios with futures and swaps. Basis risk: futures vs cash (CTD), swaps vs Treasuries (swap spread). Choosing a hedge universe: what traders actually use for long-end duration (UB, WN, 20y/30y swaps, cash bonds). Position limits, no-short rules for cash, desk mandates. Convex optimization basics: linear vs quadratic programs, L1 penalties for cost, feasibility and infeasibility reporting. cvxpy problem formulation and solver choice (Clarabel, OSQP); rounding after the solve. Explaining a solution to a trader: why these instruments, what was traded off.

concepts.title: Data and operations
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover: security master — CUSIP/ISIN, reference data fields, handling new issues and reopenings. Positions from PMS/OMS: trade date vs settlement date positions, books and desks. EOD marks and price sources (Bloomberg BVAL, ICE, internal marks); close times and snapshot timing. Public data for prototyping: U.S. Treasury daily par yield curve, FRED, NY Fed SOFR. Data quality checks: stale quotes, missing tenors, curve sanity (no negative forwards where unexpected). Start-of-day process: EOD cutoff, batch timing, what happens when inputs fail validation.

concepts.title: Governance and model risk
concepts.brief: Pointers to cover: model risk management (Fed SR 11-7) — model inventory, validation, ongoing monitoring; what a bank will ask before using the engine. Independent price verification and reconciling the engine's risk with the bank's official risk system. Risk limits: DV01 and key-rate limits, who sets them, how breaches are escalated. Segregation of duties: analysis vs execution vs approval. Audit trail and record-keeping expectations for trading decisions. AI-specific controls: human approval, explainability of agent output, no model-computed numbers.

notes: This book is the domain-knowledge study guide for a team building a Fixed Income Fork-Based Risk Engine, assuming working knowledge of bonds and swaps. The requester's seed outline frames each item as 'a pointer to study, not an explanation' — the book should turn those pointers into real explanations. Each concept entry's brief carries the requester's exact bullet list for that chapter; cover them all. Suggested reading from the request (use as research anchors and a further-reading list): Tuckman & Serrat, 'Fixed Income Securities' (rates, risk measures, swaps); Burghardt et al., 'The Treasury Bond Basis' (Treasury futures and CTD); Hagan & West, 'Interpolation Methods for Curve Construction' (curve construction paper); Ballabio & Balaraman, 'QuantLib Python Cookbook' (QuantLib in Python); Boyd & Vandenberghe, 'Convex Optimization' and the cvxpy docs (convex optimization); Federal Reserve SR 11-7, 'Guidance on Model Risk Management' (model risk).
